summary: Nae Ionescu was a philosopher and religious studies scholar. He studied at the University of Bucharest (~1908–1912), the University of Göttingen (~1913–1914), and the University of Munich (~1914–1919), later holding a post at the University of Bucharest (~1920–1940).
Nagin J. Shah worked in Indology and philosophy. He succeeded Dalsukh Malvania and served as Acting Director at the L.D. Institute of Indology (attested 1968).

Nalinaksha Dutt was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Chittagong College, Presidency University, University of Calcutta (Ph.D.), and University of London (D.Litt). He served as Head of Pali at Calcutta (~1923–1958) and President of The Asiatic Society (1959–1961).

Nalini Balbir is an Indologist and linguist who studied under Colette Caillat (~1976–1980). She held posts at the CNRS (1982–1988), Sorbonne Nouvelle University (from 1988), and the École Pratique des Hautes Études (from 2000).

Nalini Devdas specialized in religious studies, philosophy, and Indology, earning a PhD from Concordia University (attested 2004) under Leslie Orr. She also studied under several teachers, including Paul David Devanandan, and held a post at Carleton University.

Nam-lin Hur is a scholar of Japanology, religious studies, and history. He studied at the University of Tokyo and completed his doctorate under Helen Hardacre. He was a postdoctoral fellow at Harvard and joined the University of British Columbia (attested 2000).

Naman P. Ahuja is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He earned his doctorate from SOAS University of London and has served as Professor of Indian Art and Architecture at Jawaharlal Nehru University (attested 2018).

Namgyal Rinpoche was a Buddhist studies and religious studies teacher. He studied at Jarvis Baptist Seminary, the University of Michigan, and under traditional teachers including Mahasi Sayadaw and the 16th Karmapa, later founding Kagyu Samye Ling and the Dharma Centre of Canada.

Namio Egami was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo (~1927–1930), later teaching there (~1949–1967) and serving as Director of the Ancient Orient Museum (~1978–2002).
Namita Das is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who earned her PhD at Gauhati University under the supervision of Sibnath Sarma.

Namkhai Norbu was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Derge Gonchen, Kuse Serjong Shedra, and Khamdre Shedra, and held professorships at the Italian Institute for the Middle and Far East (~1964–1992) and the University of Naples (1962–1992).

Nancy E. Levine is a scholar of Tibetology and anthropology. She held positions in anthropology at the University of California, Los Angeles, attested as Associate Professor in 1998 and Professor in 2026.

Nancy G. Lin specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. She studied at Columbia University and earned her PhD from the University of California, Berkeley. In 2026, she is attested as faculty at the Numata Center for Buddhist Translation and Research.

Nancy Hock is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, under Joanna Gottfried Williams in 1987, and was affiliated with the Asian Art Museum (attested 1987).

Nancy McCagney works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She studied under scholars including Chögyam Trungpa, Ninian Smart, and Gerald James Larson, and held a post at the University of Delaware (attested 1997).

Nandini Bhattacharyya-Panda is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. She has held posts as a Project Fellow at the Maulana Abul Kalam Azad Institute of Asian Studies (attested 2011) and as a Senior Fellow at the ICHR.
Nang Dzé Drubpé Dorjé was a scholar who studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Shechen Gyaltsab.

Nanigopal Majumdar was an archaeologist and Indologist. He served as Superintendent at the Archaeological Survey of India (1931) and Superintendent of the Archaeological Section at the Indian Museum (attested 1939).
Nantu Shaw is an Indology and philosophy scholar who served as a visiting scholar at Stony Brook University under doctoral supervisor Sthaneshwar Timalsina (attested 2026).

Naoji Okuyama is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed doctoral studies (~1980–1985) and held teaching posts (~1985–1992) at Tohoku University, later serving as a professor at Koyasan University (~1999).
